title: Podcast EP358: How Custom Silicon Development Allowed Cisco to Fuel New Innovation for Its Customers - Semiwiki
gist: SemiWiki podcast EP358 with Nick Kucharewski, SVP/GM of Cisco's silicon development organization, on why Cisco moved to in-house custom silicon (the Silicon One family) at a time when most networking vendors still bought merchant ASICs, and how a programmable network fabric lets Cisco absorb shifting AI-deployment and security requirements.

insights.claim: Cisco moved to building custom networking silicon in-house early, at a time when most other networking providers were still relying on external ASIC suppliers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Vertical silicon integration at Cisco removes merchant-ASIC vendors from part of the networking BOM — watch which merchant switch-silicon suppliers lose socket share.
insights.quote: Dan explores Cisco’s early and pioneering move to build custom silicon in-house. This happened when most other providers were using ASIC suppliers.
insights.locator: In this broad discussion, Dan explores Cisco's early...

insights.claim: Cisco's Silicon One is positioned as a single scalable and programmable networking product family spanning the company's switching and routing roadmap, run end-to-end by one silicon development organization.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A single programmable silicon family across product lines is the structural argument for Cisco margin defense in AI networking — track Silicon One design wins versus merchant alternatives.
insights.quote: Silicon One, Cisco’s uniquely scalable and programmable networking product family
insights.locator: Daniel is joined by Nick Kucharewski...

insights.claim: Owning the silicon lets Cisco ship hardware that adapts to system requirements that keep changing because of AI deployment and rising security demands, rather than freezing capability at tape-out.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Programmable fabric is the stated defense against AI workloads churning faster than silicon cycles — a claim to test against actual refresh rates of Cisco AI networking gear.
insights.quote: the ability to deliver hardware that can adapt to the ever-changing system requirements driven by AI deployment and the need for more robust security
insights.locator: Much of it relates to the ability to deliver hardware...

insights.claim: Custom silicon development is credited with giving Cisco a flexible, programmable network fabric that in turn opened new innovation opportunities for Cisco's own customers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The pitch is that customer-side innovation, not just cost, is the payoff of in-house silicon — useful framing when assessing whether Cisco can hold accounts against white-box networking.
insights.locator: Nick describes how custom silicon development allowed Cisco...

insights.claim: Nick Kucharewski, Cisco's SVP and GM for silicon development, owns end-to-end strategy, cross-functional execution, organizational alignment and the product roadmap for Silicon One — a single-owner structure for the whole silicon stack.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Concentrated ownership of strategy plus roadmap means Silicon One execution risk is tied to one leadership seat — a personnel change there is a signal worth watching.
insights.locator: Nick Kucharewski Senior Vice President and General Manager

insights.claim: Kucharewski brings over 25 years spanning chip design, engineering management, product management and general management, with product work across AI and cloud infrastructure, wireless networking, optics, enterprise switching, carrier routing and broadband access.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The breadth of the remit shows Cisco is steering Silicon One at AI/cloud infrastructure and optics as much as at classic enterprise switching.
insights.locator: His work has contributed to silicon and software product innovations
